PATIENT: SYNTHETIC PATIENT 03  MRN 9923000003  DOB 04/10/1971
PROCEDURE: Ion robotic bronchoscopy
INDICATION: 3.3 cm right middle lobe PET-avid lesion; prior treated lung cancer. Tissue diagnosis requested.
ANESTHESIA: General anesthesia with laryngeal mask airway
After informed consent and time-out, a therapeutic bronchoscope was introduced under general anesthesia with laryngeal mask airway. Airway
inspection to the first subsegmental level showed no obstructing endobronchial lesion. The Ion robotic platform was docked and a deliberate workflow
with fluoroscopy, radial EBUS, and cone-beam confirmation was performed. The target was a 3.3 cm lesion in the right middle lobe. Imaging
confirmation used CBCT. Initial fluoroscopy suggested near-target positioning. Radial probe EBUS demonstrated no clear radial image but lesion
localization felt acceptable after fluoroscopic confirmation. A cone-beam or tomographic spin was then obtained to assess tool-to-lesion relationship,
after which the catheter was adjusted as needed and repeat fluoroscopy was performed. Once tool-in-lesion or satisfactory tool-to-lesion relationship
was confirmed, lesion sampling proceeded. Samples obtained included TBNA x4; forceps biopsies x9; brushings x2; BAL x1. Technical difficulty: No.
Limitation(s): None. Associated linear EBUS staging was then performed. Surveyed stations included 7 (10.1 mm), 4R (7.2 mm), 11R (8.9 mm), 10R (7.4
mm). Sampled stations: 7 x4 (no ROSE; cytology/cell block); 4R x3 (no ROSE; cytology/cell block); 11R x4 (no ROSE; cytology/cell block). At the end of
the case, the airway was reinspected, blood/secretions were suctioned, and there was no active bleeding.
EBL: <5 mL
COMPLICATIONS: Brief SVT during procedure, self-limited after anesthetic adjustment
IMPRESSION: Successful ion robotic bronchoscopy targeting of the right middle lobe lesion. Associated EBUS staging was performed. Minor immediate
complication: brief svt during procedure, self-limited after anesthetic adjustment.
PLAN: Recover in PACU; post-procedure chest radiograph per protocol; await final pathology; integrate EBUS staging into treatment planning
